statement: n = 20 is the largest ring size computed: 4416 CPU seconds for the 88 classes, longest job 510 s (class 76), largest peak memory 2554 MB (class 76). Cost grows by a factor 14 (median over the 6 heaviest classes) from n = 18 to 20; extrapolated with each class's own factor, n = 22 needs about 16.0 CPU hours, i.e. about 8.0 h wall at 2 workers. The memory wall is the stored distance rows (one byte per cycle per rotation orbit): at n = 22 class 76 has 664183 cycles in 30229 rotation orbits, 20.1 GB of rows. Both are properties of this implementation (dense V rows per orbit, one BFS over all 2^n states per orbit), not of the rules; keeping only the weight levels the contraction actually expands (and recomputing a row on demand) would reduce the memory term; the BFS term (orbits x 2^n) remains.
